# Contributing

Thanks for being willing to contribute!

## Table of Contents

- [How to Contribute](#How-to-Contribute)
- [Contribution-Guidelines](#Contribution-Guidelines)

## How to Contribute

#### **Did you find a bug?**

- **Do not open up a GitHub issue if the bug is a security vulnerability in BitBanana**, and instead to refer to our [Security Policy](../README.md#security).

- **Ensure the bug was not already reported** by searching on GitHub under [Issues][issues].

- If you're unable to find an open issue addressing the problem, [open a new one][issues]. Be sure to include a **title and clear description**, and as much relevant information as possible.

#### **Did you write a patch that fixes a bug?**

- Open a new GitHub pull request with the patch.

- Ensure the PR description clearly describes the problem and solution. Include the relevant issue number if applicable.

#### **Do you intend to add a new feature or change an existing one?**

- Please join us on [discord][discord] and check [open issues][issues] to see what contributions are needed before tackling a task to avoid duplicate work.

#### **Do you have questions about the source code?**

- Ask any question about the BitBanana source code in [discord][discord].

## Contribution Guidelines

### Pull Requests

The `master` branch will be used for all pull requests for the time being. This may change as the repo and contributors grow.

### Style Guide

This project has lint rules and pull requests should pass before being merged. The lint rules are not final by any means and can be changed if necessary.

We also provide some code style rules within the project. Make sure your IDE is taking the provided files into consideration.
If you are using IntelliJ or Android Studio, check out the following link for selecting the projects code style: [IntelliJ Code Style][codestyle]

evidence: UtilFunctions.encodePbkdf2 constructs a javax.crypto.spec.PBEKeySpec with password, salt, iterations, and bytes * 8.
The PBEKeySpec specification requires iterationCount >= 10000 for its accepted four-argument construction event; this is a CrySL rule threshold rather than a documented Java API minimum.
A runtime execution reaching the reviewed governed call used iteration count 5000, which is below the CrySL threshold.
The reviewed method does not invoke clearPassword() on its locally constructed PBEKeySpec before returning.
The output derived from appLockDataHash is used for persisted password/PIN hash values and for comparisons during access-data checks.
migration_assessment.safe_strategy: Raise the PBEKeySpec iteration count to at least 10000 for newly written derivations and clear the local PBEKeySpec only after key derivation has consumed it. evidence: encodePbkdf2 constructs a PBEKeySpec and invokes javax.crypto.SecretKeyFactory.getInstance with the literal algorithm value "PBKDF2WithHmacSHA1", then invokes generateSecret on the resulting factory value.

The SecretKeyFactory specification governs javax.crypto.SecretKeyFactory getInstance and generateSecret events, requires Get before Gen, constrains the algorithm to its explicit allowlist, and requires speccedKey[keySpec, _] for generateSecret.
PBKDF2WithHmacSHA1 is excluded from the specification's explicit algorithm allowlist.
The runtime detector measurement recorded PBKDF2WithHmacSHA1 as the value reaching the governed call at UtilFunctions.java:94 in two application runs.
The derivation result is hex-encoded by appLockDataHash and is used in persisted app-lock credential values and comparisons against persisted values.
The supplied specification does not define speccedKey or establish that constructing a PBEKeySpec produces that predicate.
migration_assessment.safe_strategy: Replace the excluded PBKDF2WithHmacSHA1 acquisition with an allowlisted, target-provider-supported PBKDF2 PRF, and make newly persisted credential derivations distinguishable from legacy derivations. Preserve verification of existing SHA-1-derived stored values through an explicit legacy path or migration-on-success mechanism; all persistence writers and access-check readers must use the same version-selection policy.

publication_considerations.description: The existing derivation output is persisted and used for comparisons. A new PRF produces different values, so a patch must preserve access to credentials written under PBKDF2WithHmacSHA1 or deliberately authorize their invalidation. The available build, unit-test, Android-test compilation, and source recheck cannot establish compatibility with users' already persisted values.
publication_considerations.kind: Persisted credential compatibility: reviewers must verify that pre-update password, PIN, emergency-password, and emergency-PIN hash values remain usable, through an explicit legacy-verification or migration policy, before publishing the change.

publication_considerations.description: The rule establishes the permitted algorithm names, but neither repository evidence nor the cited provider documentation establishes that a particular replacement is available and accepts this KeySpec on every supported deployment. The pipeline does not run on devices or exercise platform providers.
publication_considerations.kind: Deployment provider behavior: reviewers must validate the selected allowlisted PBKDF2 algorithm and PBEKeySpec combination on supported Android/provider versions.

review_assumptions: The runtime crypto provider on supported Android versions exposes SecretKeyFactory algorithm PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256.

Coordinated AppLockUtil changes will verify unversioned persisted credentials using an explicit legacy PBKDF2WithHmacSHA1 derivation and will use UtilFunctions.appLockDataHash only for current-version credential creation or verification.

The pre-update UtilFunctions.appLockDataHash implementation derived a 32-byte PBKDF2 value using the app salt, 1,000 iterations, Android Base64 encoding, and PBKDF2WithHmacSHA1. These compatibility parameters must be checked against the pre-update implementation before merge because the supplied target source does not include that method body.

The current UtilFunctions.appLockDataHash result is a non-null encoded credential value and, after its coordinated change, uses PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 with the same salt, iteration, key-length, and encoding contract as the pre-update app-lock derivation.

Credential readers will treat a non-null result from verifyAndMigrateAppLockDataHash as successful authentication and persist that returned value; a null result means authentication failed. Writing the returned current value for an already-current credential is intentionally harmless.

The emergency-unlock path that copies EMERGENCY_PASSWORD_HASH into PASSWORD_HASH intentionally preserves the existing stored credential as part of its concealment behavior. Its eventual legacy migration remains the responsibility of PasswordEntryActivity after successful verification.
AppLockUtil.appLockDataHash(String) is available with the provided contract and returns the coordinated app-lock-v2 credential value.
PrefsUtil encrypted-preference access and editor operations no longer declare GeneralSecurityException or IOException, as required by the prior semantic validation feedback.

The emergency-unlock branch that copies an existing emergency credential preserves that existing credential verbatim because it does not derive a new credential and has no plaintext from which to create a current-format replacement.

PasswordSetupActivity.passwordCreated(String), as supplied by the coordinated file contract, is the persistence boundary for the raw values submitted by this fragment, including emergency-password creation flows.

The direct UtilFunctions.appLockDataHash call in this fragment is part of an existing credential verification path, not a credential writer; the shared plan assigns version-aware credential-reader migration changes to PasswordEntryActivity.

PrefsUtil.getEncryptedPrefs() returns an editable SharedPreferences-compatible preferences object, so calling edit().putString(...).apply() persists the migrated credential as used by the existing credential persistence flows.

AppLockUtil.verifyAndMigrateAppLockDataHash(String, String) accepts the persisted credential as its first argument and the entered raw credential as its second argument, returning null for verification failure and the current-format persisted replacement for success.

When both configured normal and emergency credentials match the entered value, migrating both successfully verified stored values preserves existing acceptance behavior while applying the approved migration-on-success policy.

evidence: KeyStoreSpec governs java.security.KeyStore and defines the accepted order Get, Load, then repetitions of either optional GetEntry followed by GetKey or SetEntry followed by Store.
CryptoManager defines keyStore as a lazy java.security.KeyStore initialized with getInstance("AndroidKeyStore") followed by load(null).

CryptoManager.getOrCreateKey invokes keyStore.getEntry(KEY_ALIAS, null), safely casts the result to KeyStore.SecretKeyEntry, and returns its secretKey when available; it does not invoke KeyStore.getKey in that method.
The reviewed getOrCreateKey trace is noncompliant with the KeyStoreSpec read-branch order because its observed GetEntry event has no following GetKey event.
The source and supplied runtime measurement do not establish successful provider selection, successful loading, alias existence, entry recoverability, or runtime entry subtype.
migration_assessment.safe_strategy: Preserve the AndroidKeyStore provider selection and its load(null) initialization, but use the KeyStore read operation that satisfies the modeled read branch and preserves the method's SecretKey-or-generation fallback contract. Do not replace or pin "AndroidKeyStore" to a desktop keystore type solely to satisfy the rule's obsolete five-type whitelist.

evidence: The reviewed fetch method constructs a SecretKeySpec with byte material derived from context.getString(R.string.key_lastLegalityUpdate) and with algorithm argument "AES".
The byte material passed to SecretKeySpec is derived from a resource value compiled into the application.
The reviewed code obtains an IV argument by calling getEncoded() on the constructed SecretKeySpec.
The same constructed SecretKeySpec and IV are used to decrypt three strings before those decrypted values are supplied to TcgpApi.getAccessToken.
The supplied SecretKeySpec specification requires an allow-listed algorithm, a non-String keyMaterial value, a length constraint, and prepared-or-randomized key material for its c1 event.
The specification does not define preparedKeyMaterial, randomized, or the evaluation of offset and len for the two-argument c1 event.
migration_assessment.safe_strategy: Replace the application-compiled byte material used for the initial SecretKeySpec with key material from a managed generated or imported SecretKey lifecycle, and do not derive the IV from that key's encoding. Before removing the legacy material, re-encrypt or otherwise replace every value that the current key/IV decrypts so the three plaintext arguments supplied to TcgpApi.getAccessToken remain unchanged under the new scheme. The rollout must preserve the existing ciphertext/key-format and access-token-input contract or explicitly rotate it with its owner.

publication_considerations.description: A reviewer must verify that all affected encrypted values are re-encrypted/replaced and that the resulting plaintext inputs remain acceptable to the access-token API. The pipeline build, unit tests, androidTest compilation, and source recheck cannot establish an external or persisted ciphertext contract.
publication_considerations.kind: Ciphertext and API-input compatibility must be preserved: replacing the fixed key material must still decrypt or validly replace the three values supplied to TcgpApi.getAccessToken, including any external payload or endpoint expectations.

publication_considerations.description: The patch must not silently change the credentials or configuration represented by the decrypted values. No supplied case policy selects a rotation or compatibility strategy; that decision requires review and is not discharged by automated validation.
publication_considerations.kind: A maintainer must choose and authorize the rollout semantics for existing encrypted material: coordinated rotation/re-encryption versus another backward-compatible migration that removes the offending static SecretKeySpec construction.

review_assumptions: The three ciphertext literals and independently stored IV values shown in this draft are the approved migration artifacts for the AndroidKeyStore alias tcgp_access_token_credentials; their actual production values must be verified before merge because no approved envelope artifacts were supplied with this target source.
The application compiles against Android API 23 or newer, where android.security.keystore.KeyGenParameterSpec and AndroidKeyStore AES generation are available.

evidence: CryptoManager imports java.security.KeyStore and initializes a keyStore field using KeyStore.getInstance("AndroidKeyStore").apply { load(null) }.
On a cache miss, getSecretKey calls keyStore.getEntry(alias, null), obtains SecretKeyEntry.secretKey when the entry has that subtype, caches it, and otherwise creates a key.

KeyStoreSpec applies to java.security.KeyStore and defines the accepted protocol Get, Load, ((GetEntry?, GetKey) | (SetEntry, Store))*; its GetEntry event is permitted only immediately before GetKey in the read branch.
The source-level KeyStoreSpec read-branch requirement is not met because the governed getEntry path has no following governed getKey invocation.
The KeyStoreSpec factory-type constraint is not met by the source argument "AndroidKeyStore" because that string is absent from the specification's five allowed type values.
getSecretKey supplies keys to the source's encryption, decryption, and HMAC initialization paths.

The supplied KeyStore specification does not establish that conforming to its GetEntry-then-GetKey model is a universal Java KeyStore runtime or security requirement; it is a CrySL typestate rule for java.security.KeyStore.

# Contributing to Feeder

Thanks for your interest in contributing! Feeder is an open-source RSS/Atom/JSONFeed reader for Android.
It is available on [F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/en/packages/com.nononsenseapps.feeder/) and
[Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.nononsenseapps.feeder.play).

---

## Getting started

Clone the repository:

```
git clone https://github.com/spacecowboy/Feeder.git
cd Feeder
```

Build and install to a connected Android device:

```
./gradlew installFdroidDebug
```

No API keys or special local configuration are required to build and run the app.

---

## Architecture overview

Feeder uses **MVVM** with a unidirectional data flow. A more detailed breakdown is available in
[`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md), which also serves as the reference for AI coding agents.

The short version:

- **`ui/compose/`** — Jetpack Compose screens and components
- **`ui/*.kt`** — ViewModels that own coroutine scopes and expose `StateFlow` to the UI
- **`archmodel/Repository.kt`** — single source of truth for all dynamic data
- **`archmodel/*Store.kt`** — domain-scoped data access (feeds, items, settings, …)
- **`db/room/`** — Room database, entities, DAOs
- **`model/`** — feed parsing, HTML, OPML, notifications

Dependency injection is handled exclusively by **Kodein DI**. Please do not introduce Hilt, Dagger,
or any other DI framework.

---

## Running tests

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| JVM unit tests only | `./gradlew test` |
| **Full test suite** (JVM + instrumented) | `./gradlew check connectedCheck` |

Instrumented tests (`connectedCheck`) use a Gradle-managed virtual device (`pixel2api30`) that is started automatically. No physical device or manually started emulator is required — just a correctly configured Android SDK.

---

## Code style

Feeder uses **ktlint**. Before opening a pull request, format your code:

```
./gradlew ktlintFormat
```

To check without modifying:

```
./gradlew ktlintCheck
```

CI will fail on unformatted code.

---

## Database schema changes

> **This is a hard rule — no exceptions.**

If your change modifies the Room database schema (adding/removing/altering tables or columns), you
**must** also provide:

1. A migration object `MIGRATION_N_N+1` in `app/src/main/java/com/nononsenseapps/feeder/db/room/AppDatabase.kt`,
   registered in the `Room.databaseBuilder` call.
2. A migration test in `app/src/androidTest/java/com/nononsenseapps/feeder/db/room/`.

Feeder has users upgrading across many versions. A missing migration causes data loss, which is a
critical bug.

---

## Commit messages

Feeder follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) with **past-tense**
descriptions (they read better in the auto-generated changelog):

```
<type>: <past-tense description>
```

Examples:

```
fix: adjusted sync frequency
feat: added article text size setting
chore: updated dependency versions
refactor: extracted feed parsing into separate class
```

Common types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`, `docs`, `test`, `style`.

---

## Translations

Translations are very welcome! The easiest way to contribute is via
[Weblate](https://hosted.weblate.org/engage/feeder/). Pull requests with translation files are also
accepted.

---

## Pull request guidelines

- Keep PRs focused — one concern per PR is much easier to review.
- Include tests for new behaviour where practical.
- Run `./gradlew ktlintFormat` before pushing.
- Follow the commit message convention above.
- If your change touches the database schema, migrations are mandatory (see above).

---

## Questions?

Open an issue on GitHub or start a discussion. The project is maintained by one person, so please
be patient — all genuine contributions are appreciated.

## Development history

### v3.x
The [original version](https://github.com/SapuSeven/BetterUntis-Legacy) of BetterUntis had many design and performance flaws.
Since development became increasingly more difficult, the project was scrapped and I started over from scratch.

Although some parts of the original code were reused, the codebase was entirely switched to Kotlin.
Kotlin has many features and libraries that immensely help to communicate with the Untis API and process the timetable data.

Another major change is the use of a custom WeekView (based on [Till Hellmund](https://github.com/thellmund)'s fork of [Android-Week-View](https://github.com/alamkanak/Android-Week-View)) for the timetable display.
This also improved performance by a lot.

### v4.x
This major version updated the WeekView component again to be based entirely on Jetpack Compose.
Since the rest of the app was already built on Compose, this made it easier to develop and improve the WeekView component.

### v5.x
This version introduces a complete architecture overhaul to follow the latest Android Jetpack guidelines.
Additionally, several components (like Untis API Client, Compose Preferences, ...) were separated to their own module
to potentially reuse them in other projects.

### Branch: develop
This branch contains the current development version. Small changes and fixes can be committed directly to this branch.

When it reaches a state ready to release, it can be merged into the **master**-branch and a new release can be published.

case_migration_policy.scope: This authorization is conditional and applies only to a digest whose value is recomputed from live data and compared against another value produced by the same code path in the same process. It does not authorize changing a digest whose value is persisted, transmitted, exported, or compared against a value produced by any other program or by an earlier release.

case_migration_policy.strategy: Replace the weak algorithm literal with a governed algorithm (SHA-256 preferred) while preserving the surrounding method signature, return type, and value-derivation shape. Both the stored comparison value and the recomputed value come from the same method, so an in-process discriminator stays correct across the change without any value migration.
case_migration_policy.finding_semantics: A confirmed algorithm-allowlist violation is a real finding even when the digest is not used for security. Do not claim a runtime security impact that the evidence does not establish, and do not treat the absence of a proven security impact as a reason to leave the governed algorithm in place.
case_migration_policy.absence_of_proof_guidance: A bounded scope analysis can never prove that no unexamined, reflective, packaged, or external consumer exists. When the examined scope is complete for the reachable callers and identified no such consumer, treat that as supporting the internal classification rather than as a compatibility blocker. Requiring proof of a universal negative would make every digest migration permanently unfixable, which is not the intent of this policy.
forbidden_changes: Do not change the method signature, return type, or the number of digest bytes folded into the returned value; the name may change only under a rename_safety authorization.
Do not make a function whose name states the weak algorithm (sha1, md5) compute a different digest: switch its callers to an existing correctly named function, or rename it under rename_safety.
Do not change a digest whose value names or keys stored data (a file, a database, a preferences entry) or is sent out of the process; derived_value_consumers records where it goes.
Do not migrate a digest whose expected value is produced by an external backend, another repository, or a previous release.
Do not introduce a persisted or transmitted representation of the digest that did not already exist.
Do not claim the change removes a security vulnerability when the evidence classifies the usage as non-security.
required_tests: The discriminator still reports an unmodified value as unmodified.

# Contributing

Thanks for wanting to contribute source code to Nextcloud Cookbook Android client.
That's great!

Please always create an [issue](https://github.com/lneugebauer/nextcloud-cookbook/issues) before starting a change.
This is very helpful to understand what kind of issue the pull request will solve and if your change will be accepted.

## Bugfix

Please describe the type of bug you want to fix and provide feedback on how to reproduce the problem.
I'll only accept bug fixes if I can reproduce the problem.

## Features/Improvements

Not every feature is relevant to the majority of the users.
It helps to have a discussion about a new feature before opening a pull request.

## Translations

Thank you for your interest in translating Nextcloud Cookbook Android client!
I appreciate your help in making it accessible to a wider audience.

### Weblate

I have chosen to use Weblate as a platform for translations.
Weblate provides an easy-to-use web-based interface that allows translators to collaborate and work on translations.

To get started with translating the app on Weblate, simply [visit the translation page](https://hosted.weblate.org/engage/nextcloud-cookbook/) and select your preferred language.
You can then start translating the app directly on the platform.

There are two components: [App](https://hosted.weblate.org/projects/nextcloud-cookbook/app/) and [Fastlane](https://hosted.weblate.org/projects/nextcloud-cookbook/fastlane/).

App contains all strings used in the app.

Fastlane is a collection of app store metadata that is used to submit the app to F-Droid and Play Store.

### XML

Please fork the repository, make your changes to the XML files and submit a pull request. Remember
to include information about what language it is.

All strings are located in the `res/values` directory in a file
called [`strings.xml`](https://github.com/lneugebauer/nextcloud-cookbook/blob/main/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml)
.

For different languages, you create separate directories with the appropriate language code,
e.g. `res/values-de` for German.
Copy the `strings.xml` file into each of the language-specific directories and translate the strings
into the appropriate language.

In Android Studio, you can use
the [translations editor](https://developer.android.com/studio/write/translations-editor), but you
are free to use any text editor you like.

# Contributing To Metadata Remover

👍🎉 First off, thanks for taking the time to contribute! 🎉👍

The following is a set of guidelines for contributing to [Metadata Remover](https://poopjournal.rocks/MetadataRemover/), which are hosted on [GitHub](https://github.com/Crazy-Marvin/MetadataRemover/).
These are just guidelines, not rules. Use your best judgment, and feel free to propose changes to this document in a pull request.

## What should I know before I get started?

### Code of Conduct

This project adheres to the [Contributor Covenant code of conduct](https://contributor-covenant.org/version/1/4/).
By participating, you are expected to uphold this code. Please report unacceptable behavior to [marvin@poopjournal.rocks](mailto:marvin@poopjournal.rocks).

### Contact

If you have any questions or are unsure about something just drop a line to [marvin@poopjournal.rocks](mailto:marvin@poopjournal.rocks).

### Design Decisions

If you plan to make a significant decision in how to maintain the project and what it can or cannot support please send an email beforehand. 

## How Can I Contribute?

### Reporting Bugs

This section guides you through submitting a bug report for [Metadata Remover](https://poopjournal.rocks/MetadataRemover/) software. Following these guidelines helps maintainers and the community understand your report 📝, reproduce the behavior 📱💻🎮, and find related reports 🔎.

Before creating bug reports, please check this list as you might find out that you don't need to create one. When you are creating a bug report, please include as many details as possible.

### Translating Strings

You can help to translate the app and marketing texts (e.g. Google Play description) via [Weblate](https://hosted.weblate.org/engage/metadata-remover/).

### Suggesting Enhancements

This section guides you through submitting an enhancement suggestion for [Metadata Remover](https://poopjournal.rocks/MetadataRemover/), including completely new features and minor improvements to existing functionality. Following these guidelines helps maintainers and the community understand your suggestion 📝 and find related suggestions 🔎.

Before creating enhancement suggestions, please check this list as you might find out that you don't need to create one. When you are creating an enhancement suggestion, please include as many details as possible.

### Pull Requests

+ Include screenshots and animated GIFs in your pull request whenever possible.
+ Create a [branch](https://guides.github.com/introduction/flow/) for your edit
    
### Git Commit Messages

+ Use the present tense ("Add feature" not "Added feature")
+ Use the imperative mood ("Move cursor to..." not "Moves cursor to...")
+ Limit the first line to 72 characters or less
+ Reference issues and pull requests liberally
+ When only changing documentation, include [ci skip] in the commit description
+ Consider starting the commit message with an applicable emoji:

        🎨 :art: when improving the format/structure of the code
        🐎 :racehorse: when improving performance
        🚱 :non-potable_water: when plugging memory leaks
        📝 :memo: when writing docs
        🐧 :penguin: when fixing something on Linux
        🍎 :apple: when fixing something on macOS
        🏁 :checkered_flag: when fixing something on Windows
        🐛 :bug: when fixing a bug
        🔥 :fire: when removing code or files
        💚 :green_heart: when fixing the CI build
        ✅ :white_check_mark: when adding tests
        🔒 :lock: when dealing with security
        ⬆️ :arrow_up: when upgrading dependencies
        ⬇️ :arrow_down: when downgrading dependencies
        👕 :shirt: when removing linter warnings
        
        
__Thank you so much! 😘__

## Contributing

PRs to the ```trunk``` need at least one approving review before getting merged.

Help translate the app at [Hosted Weblate](https://hosted.weblate.org/engage/metadata-remover/).

Pull requests are welcome. For major changes, please open an issue first to discuss what you would like to change.

Please make sure to update tests as appropriate.

Check out the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/Crazy-Marvin/MetadataRemover/blob/trunk/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) for details please.

evidence: MainViewModel defines companion-object property random by calling SecureRandom with a UTF-8 byte array derived from the literal "75rgu86gr59ht86".
The seed bytes passed to the construction call are compiled constant material rather than material generated or prepared at runtime.
SecureRandomSpec requires randomized[seed] before SecureRandom(byte[]) and ensures randomized[this] after the construction event.
The constant seed material fails the specification's randomized[seed] requirement at this construction call.
migration_assessment.safe_strategy: Replace the literal-seeded SecureRandom(byte[]) initialization with the rule-permitted unseeded SecureRandom() initialization, retaining the existing nextInt(int) filename-selection use. This removes the constant seed while preserving platform-selected SecureRandom negotiation and the filename format/alphabet behavior.

publication_considerations.description: The replacement removes constant seed material and may change generated filename sequences. The reviewed evidence establishes filename-generation use but does not establish all persisted or external consumers.
publication_considerations.kind: A reviewer must confirm that no persisted record, protocol participant, or external consumer relies on deterministic or previously generated filename values or sequences from this random instance. The patch must preserve the filename format and bounded alphabet behavior while permitting generated values to change.

review_assumptions: SecureRandom() obtains appropriate non-deterministic seed material from the platform provider; this change does not alter persisted file formats or public/protected APIs.

I found that the companion object initializes `SecureRandom` with UTF-8 bytes from a compiled string literal. This violates `SecureRandomSpec` because that constructor expects seed bytes from a randomized source, not fixed literal data.

I replaced the literal-seeded constructor call with `SecureRandom()`. This retains the shared random instance used for bounded filename selection and timestamps without supplying compiled seed material.

per_solution_details.error_message: invalid key size for algorithm RSA

evidence: ScepClient.CertReq creates a java.security.KeyPairGenerator for RSA, initializes it with the integer parameter isKeyLen, and invokes genKeyPair.
KeyPairGeneratorSpec requires Get, Init, Gen order and, for RSA integer initialization, permits only key sizes 3072 and 4096.
A runtime measurement observed the value 8192 at the governed initialization call in one application run.
The observed 8192-bit RSA initialization does not satisfy the KeyPairGeneratorSpec RSA key-size constraint.
The generated key pair is used to build and sign enrollment-related certificate material, and the private key is passed to enrollment and returned to callers.
The reviewed callers provide the CertReq key-length argument from either a UI spinner selection or an application-restrictions integer.
The supplied SCEP and PKCS#10 sources do not specify an application-specific RSA key-size requirement for this request.
migration_assessment.safe_strategy: Keep RSA key-size selection explicit at the CertReq boundary and constrain it to the rule-supported set {3072, 4096}; do not depend on a provider default or provider-specific acceptance of 8192. Preserve configurability only if its configured values are validated or mapped under a maintainer-approved enrollment policy.

publication_considerations.description: The rule permits two RSA sizes but does not select between them or prescribe handling for existing 8192-valued configuration. The patch must preserve the intended enrollment configuration policy.
publication_considerations.kind: A reviewer must choose and authorize the behavioral policy for currently supplied unsupported values, including whether 8192 is rejected, mapped, or whether callers/configuration are updated, and which permitted value—3072 or 4096—is the intended default.

publication_considerations.description: Generated keys are used for SCEP enrollment, certificate-request signing, PKCS#12-related flows, and installation. Generic SCEP/PKCS#10 specifications do not require a particular RSA size, but they do not establish the accepting CA's deployment-specific profile.
publication_considerations.kind: Deployment CA/profile interoperability with the selected permitted RSA size must be confirmed.

publication_considerations.description: The source selects no provider, and the supplied run does not establish provider identity or successful generation. A Gradle build and source recheck cannot establish device/provider behavior.
publication_considerations.kind: The supported Android/JCA provider must successfully initialize and generate the chosen allowed RSA size on supported devices.

review_assumptions: The approved unsupported-value policy is compatibility-preserving normalization: 3072 remains 3072, while 4096 and every other supplied value (including previously accepted 8192) normalize to 4096.
CertInstaller and ScepFragment will apply the same normalization or constrain their inputs consistently before invoking CertReq.
The approved compatibility policy is that a managed rsa-key-length value of 3072 selects 3072, while every other value is intentionally normalized to 4096.
Application restrictions may contain legacy or unsupported integer values; normalizing them to 4096 is compatible with the approved CertReq boundary policy.
The approved compatibility policy is that an explicit spinner value of 3072 remains 3072 and every other selected value, including legacy values such as 8192, is treated as 4096.
The spinner continues to provide a parseable numeric selection as required by the existing Integer.parseInt call; malformed selection handling is outside this change.
Persisted rsa-key-length values remain stored in their existing integer format; this change only normalizes the value passed to CertReq.

coordinated_edits.reason: Apply the approved compatibility-preserving key-size policy immediately before RSA initialization. A supplied value of 3072 remains unchanged; every other value, including legacy 8192, becomes 4096, ensuring only allowed values reach KeyPairGenerator.initialize(int) without rejecting existing callers.

per_solution_details.explanation:
<!-- pr-title: Normalize RSA key lengths before initialization -->
Today, `CertReq` passes `isKeyLen` directly to an RSA `KeyPairGenerator`; an observed value of 8192 produced an invalid key-size error. This violates the analysis tool’s `KeyPairGeneratorSpec` usage rule for RSA integer key sizes.

I now preserve 3072 and map every other requested value, including legacy 8192, to 4096 before RSA initialization. I applied the same translation in managed restrictions and the key-length spinner so callers follow the same behavior. This is safe because unsupported values no longer reach `KeyPairGenerator.initialize(int)` without rejecting existing callers.
